description: Review contrast, labels, target spacing, focus order, zoom, state communication and reading structure.

prompt:
Act as a senior product designer.

Task: Review a design for accessibility.

Input context:
- DESIGN: [DESIGN]
- TASKS: [TASKS]
- TARGET STANDARD: [TARGET STANDARD]

Review contrast, labels, target spacing, focus order, zoom, state communication and reading structure. Separate design-level concerns from implementation tests. Prioritise issues and provide verification steps; do not certify WCAG conformance from an image alone.

Make the output practical, reviewable and appropriate to the supplied context.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## Design review checklist
A pale placeholder cannot replace a persistent label. Pair error colour with explanatory text and reserve space for feedback. Confirm logical reading order when cards stack. Inspect target spacing and focus treatment in all states. Contrast calculations, screen-reader checks and real interaction testing remain necessary before any accessibility compliance statement.
